title: Applied ML: Regression Triage and Quantization Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook defines the end-to-end process for detecting, triaging, and mitigating quality regressions detected by the Applied ML eval harness, with a focused subsection on quantization-related regressions and safe rollout practices for quantized model variants. It is intended for Applied ML, Serving Runtime, SRE, and Product owners.

Goals

- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-fix model quality regressions (target: MTTR < 6 hours for high-severity regressions).
- Provide a repeatable triage path that distinguishes data, prompt, model, and quantization regressions.
- Provide safe rollout/rollback steps for quantized models and runtime kernel/compilation changes.

Scope

This doc covers:
- Nightly and on-demand eval harness alerts.
- Prompt-set and benchmark failure modes.
- Model onboarding checklists relevant to regression discovery.
- Quantization profile testing, metrics, and rollout guidelines.
- Communication and escalation templates.

Ownership and Contacts

- On-call (Applied ML): primary triage owner for eval failures.
- Serving Runtime (kernel/quantization): responsible for quantization profiles, performance regressions, and kernel fixes.
- Eng-SRE: responsible for alerts, infra, and capacity-related regressions.
- Product (feature owner): decision-maker for release vs rollback when regressions affect customer-facing features.

Definitions and Severity Levels

- Regression: statistically significant drop in one or more eval metrics vs the pinned baseline for a model-version/prompt-set combination.
- Severity P0 (High): >5% absolute drop in core metrics (or model hallucinations causing incorrect customer-visible outputs) across production prompt-set.
- Severity P1 (Medium): 1-5% metric drop or increase in hallucination rate for internal prompts.
- Severity P2 (Low): <1% metric drift or isolated prompt-set failures.

Detection Sources

1. Nightly Eval Harness: runs full prompt-set suite for each pinned model version and quantization variant.
2. On-demand regression tests: triggered by PRs, model onboarding, or customer reports.
3. Canary/Canary-to-production monitoring: production sampling routed to new model/quantized variant.
4. Quality guardrails telemetry: user-level QoE checks and schema validators.

Key Metrics and Thresholds (table)

| Metric | Alert threshold | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| eval/accuracy_delta | > 5% (P0) | Applied ML | Core accuracy or task-specific metric |
| eval/hallucination_rate | > 2% absolute increase | Applied ML | Measured on labeled prompt-set |
| model/latency/p99 | > 2x baseline | Eng-SRE | Includes quantized variant latency regressions |
| model/throughput | < 80% expected | Eng-SRE | Affects SLA for Dedicated customers |
| eval/metric_ci_failure | any CI failure | Applied ML | Statistical significance check failed |

Note: thresholds are conservative; product owners may tighten depending on workload.

Triage Workflow (ordered steps)

1. Alert validation (On-call Applied ML)
   - Confirm eval harness alert in Datadog/observability dashboard.
   - Check related signals: production samples, rollout metrics, and Canary metrics.
   - Attach initial context to the incident: model-version, quantized-variant, prompt-set id, commit hash, and recent PRs.

2. Reproduce locally (Applied ML)
   - Run eval-harness locally against the reported model/version and quantization profile.
   - Command example: eval-harness run --model-id rwd/model-v2 --variant quant-4bit --prompt-set prompts/faq-suite --output ./repro.json
   - If reproducible, collect full outputs and diffs vs baseline: 
     - eval/harness produces JSON lines with per-prompt metrics; use the included diff tool: eval-harness diff baseline.json repro.json --top 20

3. Classify regression cause
   - Prompt-related: failing only on one prompt-set or due to prompt formatting changes.
   - Data drift: new distribution in production inputs not covered by eval prompt-sets.
   - Model-change: model architecture or weights change (check model artifact digest).
   - Quantization/regression: failures only on quantized variant, or accuracy drops concurrent with quantization commit.

4. If quantization suspected, run quantization validation suite (Serving Runtime / Applied ML)
   - Run the quantization profile test harness: quant-test run --model rwd/model-v2 --profile qprofile/trimmed-4bit --prompt-sets all --metrics accuracy,perplexity,hallucination --output ./qtest.json
   - Compare against FP16 baseline using: quant-test compare --baseline baseline-fp16.json --candidate qtest.json

5. Mitigation decision (Product + Owners)
   - Temporary mitigation options: disable quantized variant in routing policy, fallback to FP16 variant, or pin traffic to previous model version.
   - If severity P0: initiate rollback to previous pinned variant and open postmortem.

6. Root cause analysis and fix (cross-team)
   - If quantization algorithm issue: Serving Runtime to reproduce and create patch/alternative profile.
   - If kernel/runtime bug: Eng-Serving-Runtime and Eng-SRE coordinate a patch and hotfix release.

Quantization Testing and Profile Checklist

- Test sets: at minimum run full benchmark suite: industry-bench, product-critical prompt-sets, and adversarial prompt-set.
- Metrics collected: accuracy, top-k overlaps, perplexity, hallucination rate, and latency (p50/p90/p99).
- Validation criteria: no metric drop > 1% vs FP16 baseline on product-critical prompts, hallucination rate change < 0.5% absolute, and p99 latency within 1.5x baseline.
- Canary traffic: start at 0.5% sampled traffic for 24 hours, increase to 5% for 48 hours, then to 25% before full rollout.

Safe Rollout Procedure for Quantized Variants (numbered)

1. Pre-checks (before any traffic)
   - CI pass for quantization tests, no CI statistical failures.
   - Performance validation on dedicated infra (GPU/CPU profiles).
   - Approval from Applied ML and Product owners.

2. Canary stage
   - Create deployment: deploy quantized variant in 'canary' pool.
   - Routing: set traffic policy to route 0.5% weighted traffic.
   - Monitor: automatically run production-sampled evals and compare metrics hourly.

3. Gradual ramp
   - If metrics stable for 48 hours, increase to 5% then 25%. Maintain rollback guardrails at each step.

4. Full rollout
   - After 7 days of stability at 25%, consider 100% rollout with post-rollout monitoring for 14 days.

Rollback and Contingency

- Immediate rollback if any of the following occur: P0 regression detected in production-sampled eval, p99 latency > 2x baseline, or sustained error rate increase > 1%.
- Rollback steps: update routing policy to pin traffic to FP16 or previous model version, evacuate canary pool, and mark deployment as failed in release tracker.

Communication and Postmortem

- Use incident channel #applied-ml-incident for real-time coordination.
- Postmortem template: summary, timeline, root cause, impact scope, corrective actions, and owners. Postmortem must be published within 3 business days for P0 incidents.

Automation and Tooling Integrations

- Eval Harness: job names and scheduling: nightly-evals (00:30 UTC), pr-evals (on PR), canary-evals (hourly while canary active).
- Dashboards: pre-built dashboards: Applied ML > Regression Overview, Quantization Validation, Canary Health.
- Alert names: AppliedML-Regression-P0, Quantization-Validation-Failure, Canary-Alert-Delta.

Example Quantization Profile (JSON snippet shown as code)

- Example profile (refer to quantization-profiles repo):
  {
    "profile_name": "trimmed-4bit",
    "algorithm": "awq",
    "per_channel": true,
    "calibration_samples": 2048,
    "fallback_precision": "fp16"
  }

Operational Notes and FAQs

- Q: When should we accept a small drop in metric for a 2x latency improvement?
  - A: Product must sign-off on tradeoffs. Maintain an explicit perf/quality tradeoff doc per model.

- Q: Who approves canary traffic increases?
  - A: Applied ML owner + Product PM. For Dedicated enterprise customers, coordinate with Customer Success for risk windows.

Related pages and references

- Eval harness onboarding and regression playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-onboarding-and-regression-playbook-2026
- Quantization profiles best practices: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026

Appendix: Quick CLI Commands

- Reproduce eval: eval-harness run --model-id rwd/model-v2 --variant quant-4bit --prompt-set prompts/faq-suite --output ./repro.json
- Compare run to baseline: eval-harness diff baseline.json repro.json --top 20
- Run quant test: quant-test run --model rwd/model-v2 --profile qprofile/trimmed-4bit --prompt-sets all --output ./qtest.json

End of document.
